headline: bdnews24.com Editor Toufique Imrose Khalidi dies at 59 in London
summary: The veteran journalist and pioneer of online journalism in Bangladesh was pronounced dead at St Bartholomew’s Hospital following a brain haemorrhage.
details: Toufique Imrose Khalidi, the editor-in-chief of bdnews24.com, passed away at 2:23pm local time on Friday in London. He was 59 years old.
Khalidi was admitted to St Bartholomew’s Hospital on Thursday night after suffering a brain haemorrhage, according to reports.
Political leaders and media peers have expressed deep shock, describing his passing as an 'irreparable loss' and a 'massive void' in the country's media landscape.
He is remembered as a pioneer of online and digital journalism in Bangladesh, known for his uncompromising professionalism and devotion to objectivity.
Jatiya Party Chairman GM Quader hailed him as a distinguished media personality who did journalism with courage and dedication.
BNP leaders, including Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi, called him an honest and courageous journalist who set a level of professionalism for future generations.
Former planning minister MA Mannan and other political figures described him as a high-calibre professional and a true patriot.
Khalidi also edited a milestone book on the Liberation War and the struggle for independence, further cementing his legacy in Bangladeshi journalism.
caption:
A pioneer of digital journalism in Bangladesh has passed away. Toufique Imrose Khalidi dies at 59.

Toufique Imrose Khalidi, the editor-in-chief of bdnews24.com, passed away at 2:23pm local time on Friday in London. He was 59 years old.

Khalidi was admitted to St Bartholomew’s Hospital on Thursday night after suffering a brain haemorrhage, according to reports.

Political leaders and media peers have expressed deep shock, describing his passing as an 'irreparable loss' and a 'massive void' in the country's media landscape.

He is remembered as a pioneer of online and digital journalism in Bangladesh, known for his uncompromising professionalism and devotion to objectivity.

Jatiya Party Chairman GM Quader hailed him as a distinguished media personality who did journalism with courage and dedication.

BNP leaders, including Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi, called him an honest and courageous journalist who set a level of professionalism for future generations.

Former planning minister MA Mannan and other political figures described him as a high-calibre professional and a true patriot.

Khalidi also edited a milestone book on the Liberation War and the struggle for independence, further cementing his legacy in Bangladeshi journalism.

headline_marked: Uranium for Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant [[arrives in Bangladesh]] from Russia
headline: Uranium for Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant arrives in Bangladesh from Russia
summary: A delayed shipment of nuclear fuel for the first unit of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant has finally landed in Dhaka after airspace issues.
details: A special cargo flight carrying uranium for the first unit of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant landed in Dhaka around 11:45 pm on Friday.
The shipment arrived on a Russian-made four-engine Ilyushin Il-76 aircraft, intended to refuel the first unit of the country's only nuclear power plant.
The delivery was originally scheduled for September 24 but was delayed after Pakistan refused to grant permission for the flight to use its airspace.
Science and Technology Minister Faqir Mahbub Anam noted that while there were gaps in approval from Pakistan, clearance was eventually granted.
The flight route involved several countries, including Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Pakistan, and India, before reaching Bangladesh.
caption:
Nuclear fuel has finally landed. After a delay caused by airspace restrictions, uranium for the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant has arrived in Dhaka.

A special cargo flight carrying uranium for the first unit of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant landed in Dhaka around 11:45 pm on Friday.

The shipment arrived on a Russian-made four-engine Ilyushin Il-76 aircraft, intended to refuel the first unit of the country's only nuclear power plant.

The delivery was originally scheduled for September 24 but was delayed after Pakistan refused to grant permission for the flight to use its airspace.

Science and Technology Minister Faqir Mahbub Anam noted that while there were gaps in approval from Pakistan, clearance was eventually granted.

The flight route involved several countries, including Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Pakistan, and India, before reaching Bangladesh.
